meta.name: SolarOne GEO visibility baseline query set

clusters.brand: Brand-led — does the AI know who we are at all
clusters.category: Category-led — the buyer question with no brand in it
clusters.spec: Spec-led — a number a buyer would search for
clusters.comparison: Comparison — forced head-to-head with an incumbent
clusters.local: Non-English — the regional clusters (ar / de / fr / ru / es)

notes: Query text is what you paste into the AI, verbatim. Do not add the brand name to a non-brand query — that is coaching.
core=true marks the 11 queries that make up one full round across all 8 platforms (88 cells). Extended queries are optional and only need the top-3 platforms.

target = the page we would want the AI to cite. Since v1.10.0 (commit a0ba31e) the three purpose-built keyword landing pages were retired: /sports-lighting/ 301s to /stadium-lighting/, /football-stadium-lights/ to /projects/football/, /tennis-court-lighting/ to /projects/tennis/. Targets below are the post-consolidation URLs, all verified 200 on 2026-10-23. Do not restore the retired paths.

Football cluster gap (2026-10-23): the original set measured stadium intent seven ways and tennis once, but football -- the buyer question behind /projects/football/ -- not at all. C5 is core (full 8 platforms); C6 tests the US "field" vs "stadium" phrasing and X3 the Musco head-to-head, both extended (top-3 platforms).

queries.notes: Disambiguation probe. If the answer describes off-grid solar street lights, the wrong SolarOne won.
The entity-resolution query. Tests whether Beijing Solarone Energy Technology is the brand the AI lands on.
Bare domain. A retrieval-based AI that has the page indexed can usually describe it.
The highest-value category query. Whoever is listed here gets the inbound enquiry.

Extended. US-leaning 'field' phrasing vs C5's 'stadium' -- tests the term split on the same target.
